source.title: Focal-SAM: Focal Sharpness-Aware Minimization for Long-Tailed Classification
source.authors: Si-Cong Li; Qian-Qian Xu; Zhi-Yong Yang; Zi-Tai Wang; Lin-Chao Zhang; Xiao-Chun Cao; Qing-Ming Huang

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper and appendices; no material truncation or garbling affects the relevant sections.
record.tranche_reason: Applies sharpness-based training to long-tailed image classification and reports Hessian sharpness measures and held-out accuracy, but does not directly measure the training-test gap.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for SAM variants on long-tailed datasets and relates Hessian sharpness to generalization. It does not test random-label memorization, interpolation, architecture comparisons, optimizer comparisons, batch-size effects, dropout, or removal of memorized examples. Its sharpness measure and evaluation do not directly test the magnitude-aware sharpness versus train-test-gap relation in V7.
record.test_reason: The study uses the flatness–generalization premise to develop Focal-SAM and evaluates its performance. Its Hessian eigenvalues, traces, and balanced test accuracies do not test V7's magnitude-aware perturbation measure or its correlation with training–test gaps. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that Focal-SAM balances head- and tail-class flatness, improves long-tailed recognition, and admits a tighter theoretical generalization bound. They also emphasize greater efficiency than CC-SAM and improved domain-shift performance. Their claims of consistent superiority have exceptions in the reported tables.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a focal-weighted sharpness penalty with SGD for long-tailed classification; evaluates balanced test accuracy and Hessian measures rather than random-label memorization or train-test gaps.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported sharpness results differ by method and class group: ImbSAM flattens tail classes but sharpens head classes relative to SAM; Focal-SAM reports lower Hessian sharpness for both groups. Performance also varies with the focal hyperparameters γ and λ, and with dataset and imbalance ratio.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR-10 LT with VS loss, ImbSAM lowers tail-class Hessian sharpness but raises head-class sharpness relative to SAM. Focal-SAM lowers tail-class measures relative to SAM and head-class measures relative to ImbSAM.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAM variants produce different class-wise Hessian sharpness in long-tailed image classification.

fits_no_version.finding: The performance tables generally favor Focal-SAM, with exceptions. For example, CIFAR-10 LT CE at IR200 gives 71.7% balanced test accuracy for Focal-SAM versus 72.6% for ImbSAM.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Class-weighted sharpness penalties can improve balanced held-out accuracy in long-tailed classification, with gains depending on the training setting.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 267, 2025
record.problems: The relevant Hessian comparisons are figure-based without numerical values or reported uncertainty. The paper does not report training-test gaps, so these results cannot establish that sharpness measures track that gap.
record.rows_left_out: No reported result directly measures a version's named behavior. The extracted Hessian comparisons are the relevant class-wise measurements; other performance tables compare long-tailed test accuracy but do not measure training-test gap.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the paired natural-label versus random-label held-out comparison.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects within a workload under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and removal with weight decay.

Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, training–test gaps among similarly fitted networks, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures. Hessian measurements and a PAC-Bayesian bound do not establish these relationships.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Correct V7 from tested_not_extracted to not tested. R1–R5 can remain ancillary findings but provide no version-linked verdict evidence. Additional performance and Hessian results are outside the versions and already covered by rows_left_out, so they do not require missing entries.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label held-out accuracy alongside it.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and test-error trends.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization comparisons.
Large versus small batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout interventions and their effects on held-out error.
The paper measures Hessian eigenvalues and trace, but does not measure the train-test gap, magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, or rank gap sizes across networks.
Removing memorized training examples and comparing retraining outcomes.
